questions.prompt: What early clue shows Pip that the Fog Marsh is spreading?
choices: The mushrooms at the edge were going out.
New trees at the edge were growing taller.
The Crystal Stream was flowing backward.
questions.answer: The mushrooms at the edge were going out.
questions.rationale: The fog had crept closer and was not stopping while the mushrooms at its edge went out; these changes at the boundary show Pip that the Fog Marsh was spreading.
questions.evidenceText: By the end of the week, the fog had crept closer. The mushrooms at the edge were going out. One by one. The fog was not stopping.

questions.prompt: Why has the marsh spirit's home grown smaller each year?
choices: Moonwood creatures left more things at its edges every year.
The spirit moved its boundary toward the Oak each year.
Pip took away the stones at its boundary each year.
questions.answer: Moonwood creatures left more things at its edges every year.
questions.evidenceText:
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."

supportingEvidence.evidenceText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.

questions.prompt: What do the stones around the marsh help everyone remember?
choices: Sharing a forest means respecting each home's space.
The fog stopped because the marsh spirit moved away.
The new boundary gave Moonwood more room than the marsh.
questions.answer: Sharing a forest means respecting each home's space.
questions.rationale: Fern admits that Moonwood creatures left things without thinking, and Luna marks a boundary so they leave space for both places; this shows sharing a forest means respecting each home's space.
questions.evidenceText:
"The marsh is the marsh," said Luna.
"Moonwood is Moonwood."
"And we leave space for both."

supportingEvidence.evidenceText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
